articles.headline: Sources: Jaguars LT Harrison out for season after surgery reveals torn ACL
articles.description: Jaguars left tackle Anton Harrison will miss the rest of the season because of a torn ACL in his right knee, league sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
articles.headlineJa: 情報筋によると、ジャガーズのLTハリソン、手術で前十字靭帯断裂が判明し今季絶望
articles.descriptionJa: ジャガーズのレフトタックル、アントン・ハリソンが右膝の前十字靭帯断裂により今シーズンの残り試合を欠場することが、リーグ関係者からNFLネットワークのイアン・ラポポートに伝えられた。
articles.body:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- Jacksonville Jaguars left tackle Anton Harrison will miss the rest of the season because of a torn ACL in his right knee, league sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

Harrison had arthroscopic surgery Thursday, which was when the extent of the injury that Harrison suffered during the Jaguars' Week 5 victory over Philadelphia was revealed. The team had already placed Harrison on injured reserve on Oct. 13.

Harrison, 24, was hurt while blocking on a running play, a sweep to the right by Bhayshul Tuten. Harrison appeared to grab his right knee after disengaging from a block and went down to the ground. He left the field on a cart.

Harrison, the 27th overall pick in 2023, was moved from right tackle to left tackle during training camp. He ranked 39th among offensive tackles with an 83.7% pass block win rate, four spots below Jaguars right tackle Cole Van Lanen (84.4%). The Jaguars picked up Harrison's fifth-year option in April.

articles.headline: What to know for Week 7: Start Stroud, one WR to trade for and one to trade away
articles.description: Faced with some tough start/sit decisions ahead of Week 7? Adam Rank has you covered at every position.
articles.headlineJa: 第7週の重要ポイント：ストラウドを起用せよ、獲得すべきWRと放出すべきWR
articles.descriptionJa: 第7週を前に、スタメンかベンチかの難しい判断に悩んでいませんか？アダム・ランクが全ポジションの指針を解説します。
articles.body:
It has been a surprising start to the NFL season. The Minnesota Vikings are one of three undefeated teams, the Los Angeles Rams are in last place in the NFC West, and the Dallas Cowboys are not playing great football. That last note might not be much of a surprise. What is surprising is that the Cowboys challenged an incomplete pass late in the fourth quarter when George Pickens just missed on a connection with Dak Prescott. 

I mean, come on, Dallas. You thought you were going to win a challenge on a dubious catch interpretation at Lambeau Field? Do you not even know your own history? That's like pretending you didn't realize Tom Landry wore fedoras on the sideline. 

But my favorite storyline so far this season is the Cleveland Browns, a team that could finish with a top-10 pick in next year's draft. To be fair, that's not normally surprising for the Browns, but the real surprise is that it's the pick they received from the Rams in the Myles Garrett trade. I mean, if the Browns make the playoffs and get a top-10 pick, that might be the biggest moment in Cleveland sports history since the Miz won his first WWE title in 2010. 

The only problem I have with the Browns -- alright, fine, not the only one -- is that they don't have a truly reliable fantasy option. I suppose it could be rookie WR Denzel Boston, who has a great matchup this week against Tennessee Titans cornerback Cor'Dale Flott, who has allowed 1.72 yards per route covered. Boston also has six end zone targets. A great play for traditional fantasy leagues and not a bad option for an anytime touchdown, either. 

Here are some other notes that you might find useful this week. 

Quarterback notes

C.J. Stroud is a quarterback you can rely on for the rest of the season. And the Houston Texans' matchup with the New York Giants this week is great. The Giants allow more than 18 fantasy points per game to the position and nearly nine air yards per attempt. It's a great spot for Stroud, and you can start him the rest of the way.

We've loved Aaron Rodgers ... well, at least for fantasy purposes over the last month. We started to see some worrying signs last week against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, although a late rally allowed him to have a decent fantasy performance. But the New Orleans Saints have recorded 19 sacks and 6.4 yards per attempt this season. I'm not saying you need to bench him, but the Pittsburgh Steelers' matchup is not quite as appealing as it might seem. 

Running back notes

I keep hearing the Las Vegas Raiders' Ashton Jeanty isn't so efficient. He has the highest stuff rate among qualifying running backs this season, but his receiving yardage makes him extremely valuable. 

Chase Brown has been a disappointment. His 3.5 yard per carry keeps his ceiling low. But he's another runner who can remain valuable because of his receiving production. Let's see what the Cincinnati Bengals do after the bye week before we make any big moves.

articles.headline: Soccer's main characters after UCL Matchday 3: Kane, Van Dijk, El Clasico
articles.description: Champions League Matchday 3 has come and gone, and we have some Main Character energy coming from Harry Kane, Barcelona and Real Madrid ahead of El Clasico, while Liverpool should worry about Virgil van Dijk's form.
articles.headlineJa: UCL第3節後の注目選手・チーム：ケイン、ファン・ダイク、そしてエル・クラシコ
articles.descriptionJa: チャンピオンズリーグ第3節が終了し、ハリー・ケイン、そしてエル・クラシコを控えたバルセロナとレアル・マドリードが主役級の存在感を放っている。一方で、リヴァプールはフィルジル・ファン・ダイクの調子を懸念すべきだろう。
articles.body:
By the time they were going for their third straight Champions League title in 2017-18, Real Madrid had mastered the art of easing in. In 2016-17, they finished behind Borussia Dortmund in their group and constantly needed their trademarked, late-game Real Madrid magic to secure points before igniting in the knockout rounds. For the three-peat, they finished second in their group behind Tottenham Hotspur, but mostly rolled in the spring again.

Paris Saint-Germain have certainly learned that you don't have to look your sharpest early on. Two seasons ago, in their first of what is currently a two-year title streak -- and in the first year for the expanded league phase structure -- they narrowly beat Girona in their first match and then lost three of their next four matches before finally starting to click into place in December. They won their next five Champions League matches by a combined 18 goals, knocked off top-seeded Liverpool in penalties in the round of 16 and ... mostly rolled from there.

You can play with fire without getting burned, but Luis Enrique has decided he really doesn't want to. PSG started far better last year, winning four of their first five league phase matches, and this fall they've been all business: After a 6-1 tuneup against Slovan Bratislava to start, they've beaten Manchester City and Barcelona, each by multiple goals. They were winless in their first four matches in all competitions in this campaign, but when the Champions League began, so did their season.

- UCL Power Rankings: Can anyone slow PSG down?

- Talking Points: Man United's mess, PSG lose Kvara, more

- Dawson: Who are Como, the destination club making waves

Along with a 2-2 draw between Arsenal and Bayern Munich, PSG's 4-2 win over Barcelona was the most noteworthy result of Champions League Matchday 3, even if Khvicha Kvaratskhelia's ACL tear cast a bit of a pall on the proceedings. But five teams continued their perfect starts -- PSG, Real Madrid, Liverpool, Aston Villa and Real Betis -- and all of the most likely candidates to win next week's Ballon d'Or made exciting plays.

The league phase keeps rolling, but here are soccer's five main characters as we move past Matchday 3.

Main character No. 1: Harry Kane's closing argument

The voting for this year's Ballon d'Or, which will be awarded this coming Monday, closed a while ago. While the prediction market odds were shifting toward Barca's Lamine Yamal for a while, they appear to have homed in on Bayern Munich's Harry Kane as the likely winner, and justifiably so. He simply had the best year of anyone, winning three trophies, leading England to the World Cup semifinals for a second time and -- oh yeah -- scoring 73 goals with eight assists in 65 total matches. Yamal had only 25 and 20, respectively, in the same period. articles.headline: NBA opening week intel: New trend in contract talks; OKC's pricey future
articles.description: Why star contract negotiations have shifted, why OKC is preparing for more roster changes and more intel from opening week.
articles.headlineJa: NBA開幕週の情報：契約交渉の新トレンドと、OKCの高額な未来
articles.descriptionJa: スター選手の契約交渉にどのような変化があったのか、なぜOKCがさらなるロースター変更を準備しているのかなど、開幕週の最新情報を届ける。
articles.body:
This is developing into a season of change in the NBA.

The tanking teams from last season are pivoting to full competition. Some talent has migrated to the East, and that appears to have changed the balance of power that was previously tilted to the West. And there's expansion on the horizon, and that could spur realignment.

But there's another trend from this summer and fall involving star players that seems to have and league executives and agents taking note.

Jump to a section:

Stars have one fewer negotiation tactic

The Thunder are about to get expensive

Leaguewide intel, reaction from openers

What star player contract trend is standing out?

Brian Windhorst: There were three significant instances of star players wanting a contract extension this summer and the team played hardball, a departure from recent practice.

Karl-Anthony Towns said on the record that he wanted to extend his contract and was willing to accept less than a max deal. The New York Knicks drew a line in the sand, put out a statement ending negotiations and went into the season with Towns unsettled and unhappy. He holds a $61 million player option for 2027-28 but can decline it and become an unrestricted free agent next summer.

Anthony Davis was interested in extending his contract with the Washington Wizards and, similar to Towns, has the ability to opt out for unrestricted free agency next summer. Agent Rich Paul let it be known that Davis was willing to negotiate a number below his max. But the Wizards tabled discussions, ESPN's Shams Charania reported, and wanted to see the results of the first 20 to 30 games of the season. Davis then announced he'd wait until after the season. (The Wizards did give a new $212 million contract to Trae Young, but after he'd opted out and become a free agent).

Jalen Duren, coming off an All-Star and All-NBA season, had a summer of discontent with the Detroit Pistons before agreeing to a new deal on the eve of training camp. It's a $200 million contract, but $87 million less than his max. Duren has said there are no hard feelings, but it was a brutal negotiation.

"A year or two ago, I don't think you'd have seen that. The teams would've felt too much pressure," an Eastern Conference executive told ESPN. "Being unhappy is not a negotiating position anymore."

Tim MacMahon: Well, the Los Angeles Lakers and Minnesota Timberwolves sure worked hard over the summer to make sure their superstars are happy.

The Lakers went all in to acquire Walker Kessler in a sign-and-trade -- sending two first-round picks and two swaps to the Utah Jazz for the rights to give him a four-year, $130 million deal -- primarily because they promised Luka Doncic that they would deliver him the rim-running, rim-protecting big man he desired. The Lakers have a lot of built-in advantages in terms of retaining superstars, but they are clearly prioritizing keeping Doncic content.

Minnesota also made a major roster overhaul in large part to please Anthony Edwards

articles.body:
Join the chat as ESPN fantasy football expert Eric Moody will be here to answer all of your start/sit questions and other fantasy-related queries, live from noon to 1 p.m. ET every Friday of the NFL's regular season. 

What's the latest injury buzz as kickoff time approaches? Which player is the better bet for your flex spot? Should you be considering a trade to upgrade your roster? Ask away! Our expert will try to answer as many questions as he can to get you ready for this week's action. 

More advice: Week 7 Rankings | Clay's Playbook | Cockcroft's matchup rankings

Why is my question not getting answered?

Once submitted, your question does not automatically get posted in the chat. Our moderators select which questions they wish to answer and are trying to avoid repeat questions or topics. Scroll back to see if perhaps your question (or one very similar) was answered earlier in the chat.

We are receiving thousands of questions during our hourlong Q&A session and try to get to as many as we can. However, while we appreciate every submission, there is no way we can get to every question that comes in.

articles.headline: What worked (and didn't) in 12 NBA season debuts: LeBron, LaMelo, more stars
articles.description: Which stars shined with their new teams? Which might want a do-over? Ben Golliver examines 12 opening week debuts.
articles.headlineJa: NBAシーズン開幕戦12選手の振り返り：レブロン、ラメロらスター選手たちの成否
articles.descriptionJa: 新チームで輝いたスターは誰か？やり直したいと感じているのは誰か？ベン・ゴリバーが開幕週の12選手のデビュー戦を分析する。
articles.body:
Newly minted Portland Trail Blazers guard Ja Morant said it best Wednesday: "You only get one chance at a first impression."

Though the Blazers were one of several teams to ace their season openers, there were also plenty of stars who might want a do-over. After all, Jayson Tatum's Boston Celtics blew a 22-point lead to the Pistons, San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama shot 1-for-13 in a loss to the rival Oklahoma City Thunder, and Giannis Antetokounmpo's Miami Heat were blown off their home court by the Minnesota Timberwolves.

Let's run through the NBA's opening week action -- through Thursday, every team will have played at least once -- with an eye toward the first impressions made by key players suiting up for new teams this season. Which ones launched with ease, and which succumbed to false starts?

Jump to a season debut

Great: Kawhi | Dame | Kessler | OKC starting 5

Good: LaMelo | LeBron | AD | PG-13 | Garland

Rough: Giannis | Yaxel vs. Luka | Miles Bridges

Great first impressions

Kawhi Leonard, Raptors

The schedule-makers gifted Leonard a home opener against the lowly Chicago Bulls on Wednesday, and the two-time Finals MVP took full advantage. Leonard wasted no time moving past a tumultuous summer marked by a delayed trade and the NBA's lengthy salary cap circumvention investigation, enjoying a hearty welcome back from the Toronto crowd before scoring 23 points and snagging four steals in a blowout victory.

The scariest part for East rivals: Leonard didn't have his signature midrange jumper dialed in and played only 24 minutes, yet the Raptors still managed a 43-point margin of victory that tied for the fifth largest in franchise history.

Toronto ran up the score with excellent balance across its starting lineup, as Leonard, Scottie Barnes, RJ Barrett and Immanuel Quickley each surpassed 20 points. How high can Leonard lift an offense that ranked 15th last season?

Damian Lillard, Trail Blazers

The Blazers' icon spent Wednesday putting his career back on track after a forgettable two-year detour with the Bucks and an Achilles injury that sidelined him last season. In his first game for Portland since 2023, the nine-time All-Star guard provided such an emotional jolt that the Blazers stormed out to a preposterous 21-0 lead and cruised to a 124-83 blowout of the Phoenix Suns.

No one will argue with the results from the opener, but it remains an open question whether Lillard and Morant are the ideal starting backcourt for Portland. Against Phoenix, Lillard scored 25 points and hit six 3-pointers, and Morant added 14 points and eight assists in only 23 minutes.

Tougher tests await: The Suns lack big and physical perimeter playmakers capable of exploiting Portland's undersized guards. But it's nice to see Lillard back where he belongs in Rip City.

articles.headline: João Pedro: I told Cole Palmer 'I didn't want to take his spot' at Chelsea
articles.description: João Pedro has said that a "friendship was born" when he assured Cole Palmer that he wasn't coming to Chelsea to steal his place in the team.
articles.headlineJa: ジョアン・ペドロ「コール・パーマーに、彼のポジションを奪いたいわけではないと伝えた」
articles.descriptionJa: ジョアン・ペドロは、チーム内での地位を奪うためにチェルシーに来たのではないとコール・パーマーに伝えたことで、「友情が生まれた」と語った。
articles.body:
João Pedro has said that a "friendship was born" when he assured Cole Palmer that he wasn't coming to Chelsea to steal his place in the team.

João Pedro was named Chelsea's Player of the Season in 2025-26 after recording 20 goals and nine assists in 50 appearances, following his move to the Blues from Brighton in 2025.

This season under Xabi Alonso's leadership, João Pedro and England pair Palmer and Morgan Rogers have formed a fearsome attacking trio.

João Pedro told ESPN that the good atmosphere in the Chelsea dressing room has helped his evolution into a No. 9: "I think so, yes -- especially here at Chelsea, where I'm surrounded by world-class players like Cole Palmer, Reece [James] and Moises Caicedo.

"I think my adjustment went well because it had been a while since there was a No. 9 here. Ever since my time at Brighton, I'd been keeping an eye on that spot -- even when I played against them, I knew it could be an opportunity for me -- and, thank God, when I arrived, Cole was a great friend to me; he reached out to me and talked to me.

"I told him I was coming to help, that I didn't want to take his spot -- nothing like that.

"And that's where a friendship was born that we carry on both on and off the field. And I think what helps me a lot -- and now Morgan [Rogers] too -- is that we have a really great friendship on and off the field; we're always joking around.

"I think that's why -- I think the players were really friendly toward me when I arrived; they welcomed me with open arms, wanted to help me, and were willing to do so -- so I think that's why I adapted so well."

- Jordan Henderson, the Premier League's oldest player, is becoming undroppable for Chelsea

- Chelsea's Emi Martínez has jaw surgery, will be 'back in a few weeks'

- Jordan Henderson not giving up on England after Chelsea revitalisation

Despite his strong start in London last season, João Pedro, 25, was surprisingly left out of Brazil's 2026 World Cup squad by Carlo Ancelotti.

In just six Premier League appearances this campaign, he has five goals and three assists.

"At Chelsea I feel very comfortable," the Brazilian said. "It's a different season, with a coach who gives me a lot of confidence, and I think that's a big part of my performance so far this season."

Chelsea, fourth in the Premier League, appear to be benefitting from Alonso's preferred tactical 3-4-2-1 formation and so is João Pedro.

"I think it does make it easier," he said. "I have Cole and Morgan there to help me, to feed me the passes -- you can see that the start of the season has been really good. So I think it's going to be a really good season for us."

João Pedro has come a long way during his time in England, after starting at Watford, then joining Brighton and eventually moving to Chelsea.

articles.headline: Betting buzz: Sportsbooks, bettors join the National Tight Ends Day frenzy
articles.description: On the fourth Sunday of every October since 2018, bettors and books alike celebrate National Tight Ends Day.
articles.headlineJa: ベッティング・バズ：ブックメーカーとベッターが「ナショナル・タイトエンド・デー」の熱狂に参戦
articles.descriptionJa: 2018年以来、毎年10月の第4日曜日には、ベッターとブックメーカー双方が「ナショナル・タイトエンド・デー」を祝う。
articles.body:
Everything that happens in sports has additional context when viewed from a sports betting perspective. From season-changing injuries to record-setting moments and so much more, the sports news cycle will constantly and significantly affect the sports betting industry.

Our NFL betting buzz file, with contributions from David Purdum, Doug Greenberg and others, aims to provide fans a look at the sports betting stories that are driving the conversation throughout each week of the season. 

Key links: NFL futures | Awards odds | Sports betting home | DraftKings 

Oct. 23: Sportsbooks, bettors join the National Tight Ends Day frenzy

By Doug Greenberg

In 2018, the Supreme Court struck down the Professional and Amateur Sports Protection Act, clearing the way for states to legalize sports betting nationwide. That same year marked the beginning of another momentous occasion that has become a stalwart of NFL betting every season.

On the fourth Sunday in October -- Oct. 25 in 2026 -- the NFL celebrates National Tight Ends Day, a tongue-in-cheek commemoration of football's most underappreciated skill position. Since San Francisco 49ers tight ends Garrett Celek and George Kittle helped bring the honorary day to life eight years ago, it has become a staple of the betting world, with bookmakers taking extra notice and bettors staking extra cash backing players of the position.

"National Tight Ends Day has become a fun day for football fans, and we've seen the excitement around it grow each year," DraftKings director of sports operation Johnny Avello told ESPN via email. "This is a prime example of a way to have fun with the content on our platform."

The sportsbook noted that it sees more engagement on tight end player props on National Tight Ends Day than in any other week of a given season. On the day last season (Oct. 28), Hard Rock Bet says it saw tight ends account for 25% of all player prop selections compared to 11% the Sunday before and 9% the Sunday after. For touchdown scorer markets, that number jumped to 42% against 16% and 10% on the surrounding Sundays.

BetMGM specifically points out that its five most-bet players for props by tickets on the day in 2025 were all tight ends: Dallas Goedert, Tyler Warren, Tucker Kraft, Travis Kelce and Kittle.

Kraft celebrated by putting up a monster stat line of seven catches for 143 yards and two touchdowns in the Green Bay Packers' Week 8 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers. Caesars Sportsbook head of football Joey Feazel said that "bettors certainly prospered" by backing Kraft and that the book has had to be more aware of bettor activity during this particular Sunday.

"This week certainly will increase the amount of action on tight ends in all facets of the games, which in turn has the ability to shorten touchdown prices when the amount of action is significantly increased," Feazel said via email. "But at the end of the day it will simply be the implied probability of each TE to score a touchdown."

articles.headline: Fantasy football last-minute pickups: Cooper Jr., Rodgers among top options
articles.description: If injuries, bye weeks or tough matchups have you seeking lineup help, Matt Bowen lists potential options.
articles.headlineJa: ファンタジーフットボール直前のおすすめ補強選手：クーパーJr.やロジャースらが有力候補に
articles.descriptionJa: 怪我やバイウィーク、厳しい対戦カードなどでラインナップの調整が必要な方へ、マット・ボーウェンが潜在的な候補をリストアップする。
articles.body:
At various points during the fantasy football season, injuries, bye weeks and breaking news can cause you to need reinforcements for your fantasy lineup. Every Friday throughout the 2026 NFL season, Matt Bowen will offer some late-week pickup options at each of the primary fantasy positions to help fill those holes, with an emphasis on deeper leagues.

Because of that, this column will focus mostly on players rostered in under 50% of ESPN leagues, with occasional exceptions.

We're going heavier on wide receivers this week, with four pass catchers who can provide varying levels of upside, fantasy floors and game-plan usage. All four targets can fit into lineups this week as deeper-league WR3s. Now, we are also lighter on quarterbacks and running backs, but I wrote up a veteran signal-caller who can be played as fringe QB1. As always, we'll hit on a tight end, and there is an available defense here with a positive Sunday matchup.

Wide receivers

Jaylin Noel, Houston Texans (17.3% rostered; vs. Giants)

The Texans' pass game is rolling right now with the level of play we are seeing from quarterback C.J. Stroud, and Noel is emerging as an explosive target. Noel scored a season-high 20.7 fantasy points in the Week 6 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars, and he has caught a touchdown pass in his past two games. Plus, the Texans are dialing up targets for Noel, who has the stop-start speed to set up coverage. He's a big-play WR3 for Sunday's matchup with the New York Giants.

Omar Cooper Jr., New York Jets (33.5% rostered; vs. Dolphins)

I wrote about Cooper earlier this week after he dropped a season-high 22.3 fantasy points on the New England Patriots on Sunday (his first full game of the season). With a route tree that will get Cooper the ball in space and set him up on shot plays, the rookie out of Indiana can use his explosive ability. It's a tougher matchup this week versus a Miami Dolphins defense that ranks in the top five against wide receivers, but Cooper also has the traits to be schemed on manufactured touches. He's an upside WR3 in the lineup.

Malik Washington, Miami Dolphins (36.3% rostered; at Jets)

I thought the roster percentage would jump a little higher on Washington, but we'll continue to write about him in this space. Yes, Washington has a limited ceiling due to a lack of touchdown production, however, he has a solid floor in deeper formats. Washington has scored 11 or more points in three straight games, and the Dolphins scheme for him out of multiple alignments and roles. Washington has caught 16 of 23 targets over his past three games and also has five carries for 26 yards. He's a WR3 for the matchup with the Jets.

Flournoy has passed tight end Jake Ferguson as the No. 3 target in Dallas behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. Flournoy scored a season-high 17 points in the Week 6 loss to Green Bay, catching seven of nine targets for 40 yards and a touchdown. Flournoy has

articles.headline: Don't be surprised if ... Rodgers is a top-12 QB, Skattebo rebounds
articles.description: Don't be surprised if Aaron Rodgers' strong play continues and Cam Skattebo bounces back in Week 7.
articles.headlineJa: こうなっても驚くな…ロジャースがトップ12のQB入り、スカッテボが復活
articles.descriptionJa: アーロン・ロジャースの好調が続き、カム・スカッテボが第7週に巻き返す展開になっても驚かないでほしい。
articles.body:
Each week in the NFL is its own story -- full of surprises, both positive and negative -- and fantasy football managers must decide what to believe and what not to believe moving forward. Perhaps we can help. If any of these thoughts come true ... don't be surprised!

NOTE: All mention of fantasy points is for PPR formats, unless otherwise mentioned.

Don't be surprised if ... Pittsburgh Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers finishes among the top 12 QB options

We must give credit to Rodgers for averaging 20.6 fantasy points over the past four games and throwing 11 touchdown passes in that span. The season numbers for the 42-year-old Rodgers may be a bit misleading, since he scored only 3.98 points in Week 2 against the New England Patriots. He is completing only 61.4% of his passes overall, which would be his worst figure since 2015. Five interceptions in six games? That's not normal, either. Still, only 13 quarterbacks boast more fantasy points this season!

Fantasy managers have some legitimate complaints about the Steelers, starting with what is an annoying running back timeshare (just let Jaylen Warren have the touches!). And many cannot forgive the wasted draft pick on offseason acquisition Michael Pittman Jr. But Rodgers is overachieving, based on recent seasons. His last season among the top 10 fantasy QB scorers came in 2021 with the Green Bay Packers. He was league MVP. Rodgers was the No. 13 QB the following season.

There are negatives here: Rodgers is about as immobile as possible, with only 17 rushing yards, and nobody has lost more yards via sacks. He has a pedestrian 47.0 QBR that ranks 22nd, and he is averaging only 6.4 yards per attempt.

However, there are positives: Rodgers is throwing a lot. He is on pace for 660 pass attempts, which would be a career high by 50 attempts. Other than 2023, when he was injured five minutes into the season, Rodgers has been durable. He plays every game. Some of the current top 15 QBs in fantasy points per game are not durable (Lamar Jackson, Jayden Daniels) or could lose their role to younger players (Kirk Cousins, Jacoby Brissett).

Who needs Pittman? Rookie Germie Bernard is the new top target and is working well with DK Metcalf, even while averaging only 9.5 yards per catch (same as Courtland Sutton, ew) and ranking 47th in yards after the catch. Sure, we would like more connections down the field, but the volume is there. Rodgers boasts running backs, wide receivers and tight ends to target, and the schedule (including this week against the New Orleans Saints in Paris) isn't terribly challenging. It's all working well enough that Rodgers should be rostered in more leagues.

articles.headline: Maxey, Sixers turn Philly boos into cheers in 29-point comeback over Cavaliers
articles.description: Booed after trailing by 24 at the half, the Sixers rode a game-high 32 points from Tyrese Maxey to erase a 29-point deficit and stun the Cavs 114-106 on Thursday.
articles.headlineJa: マクシーとシクサーズ、29点差をひっくり返す逆転劇でフィラデルフィアのブーイングを歓声に変え、キャバリアーズに勝利
articles.descriptionJa: 前半に24点差をつけられブーイングを浴びたシクサーズだったが、タイリース・マクシーがゲームハイの32得点を挙げ、29点差を跳ね返して木曜日の試合を114-106で制し、キャバリアーズを stunning（驚愕）させた。
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- The crowd at Xfinity Arena watched the Sixers cut a 29-point deficit to 10 in the third quarter Thursday night when Tyrese Maxey caught a pass from LeBron James in transition and, without taking a dribble, launched a 3-pointer.

As the ball went through the net, forcing the Cavs to call a timeout, Maxey walked toward the fans behind the scorers' table and screamed as Jaylen Brown flanked him in celebration and Joel Embiid celebrated on the other end of the court.

On a team laden with stars, it was Maxey who was the conductor of this raucous Philadelphia crowd, which followed his lead all night as the Sixers roared back to beat the Cleveland Cavaliers 114-106.

The 29-point comeback was the Cavaliers' largest blown lead and the Sixers' largest comeback in the play-by-play era. It was also the largest comeback of James' now 24-year career.

"It was just a great moment," said Maxey, who led all scorers with 32 points and six assists. "The crowd was into the game. We were just feeding off the crowd, feeding off our energy, feeding off our resilience."

Two nights after their season-opening win over the reigning champion New York Knicks, the Sixers were outclassed in nearly every way to begin Thursday night's game. They turned the ball over, couldn't get stops and missed layups.

Brown had just four points in his lowest-scoring first half at home since March 2025, while the Sixers' 15 first-half turnovers were their most in a half since January 2024. The Cavs' 69-45 halftime lead tied their largest in a season-opening half in franchise history and matched their largest halftime lead over the 76ers in franchise history.

As the first half came to a close, the Xfinity Arena crowd, most wearing the white opening night shirts with the Sixers roster and coach Nick Nurse printed on them, loudly booed.

Maxey said he challenged the group during the intermission.

"I said, well, it's time to see what we made of. Are we going to be some front-runners and only be happy when stuff is good?" Maxey said. "Or when stuff is bad, are we going to fight and be resilient? And we did that."

The Sixers responded with a quarter that Brown said "shifted the game," coming out of the break on an 8-0 run and outscoring Cleveland 37-21 in the third quarter.

Still, the Sixers went into the fourth trailing by eight. It wasn't until the 6:54 minute mark that they took the lead, when Embiid hit a 16-foot jump shot over center Jarrett Allen that gave Philadelphia its first lead, one it wouldn't relinquish.

Embiid said the team's resilience Thursday night was different from past teams he has been a part of during his 11-year Sixers career.

"No shade to anybody that's been here, but in the past, a lot of people would've just laid down and tried to move on to the next one," Embiid said.

He added: "Yeah, it was different. I said last game, after the game, it just feels different."

articles.headline: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's record 20-point streak ends in Thunder win over Nuggets
articles.description: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's historic streak of 20-point games ended Thursday night when he finished with 17 in a 96-84 win over the Nuggets.
articles.headlineJa: シャイ・ギルジャス＝アレクサンダーの20得点連続記録がストップ、サンダーはナゲッツに勝利
articles.descriptionJa: 木曜夜のナゲッツ戦で、サンダーは96-84で勝利したが、シャイ・ギルジャス＝アレクサンダーは17得点に終わり、歴史的な20得点連続記録が途絶えた。
articles.body:
Oklahoma City Thunder star Shai Gilgeous-Alexander had his first game with fewer than 20 points in nearly two years, finishing with 17 points in Thursday night's 96-84 home win over the Denver Nuggets to snap his NBA-record streak of 20-point games.

Gilgeous-Alexander, who scored 32 points in a convincing win over San Antonio on Tuesday night, shot just 6 of 19 from the field against Denver in failing to reach 20 points for the first time since Oct. 30, 2024, a streak of 141 regular-season games.

He had just under two minutes left to score three more points and extend his streak, but with Oklahoma City up 93-76 with 1:43 left, he asked Thunder coach Mark Daigneault to sub him out.

"I was going to go out there, and then I saw that [the Nuggets] had subbed, so I thought we should sub, too," Gilgeous-Alexander said. "You always treat the game with respect."

Daigneault said he wanted to leave Gilgeous-Alexander in the game because a "historic streak" was on the line and praised his star player's maturity.

"I just think of the class that it shows and the perspective that it shows for him to say, 'Hey, I'm out now. The game's calling for me to be subbed out,'" Daigneault said. "That was his substitution. And of all the things that I admire about him, that's toward the top of the list in terms of moments that I appreciate about him."

Gilgeous-Alexander, the league's two-time reigning MVP, missed all seven shots he took in the first 24 minutes Thursday night as the Thunder trailed by as many as nine points. A pair of free throws kept him from going scoreless in a half for the first time since his rookie season with the Clippers in 2019.

It marked just the fourth time in 450 games with the Thunder that he has gone without a field goal in a half. Gilgeous-Alexander scored the first basket of the third quarter to pull Oklahoma City to 48-46.

Aaron Gordon scored 20 points, and Nikola Jokic and DeMar DeRozan added 13 apiece for Denver, which was playing its first game.

A layup by Mitchell gave the Thunder a 64-62 lead -- their first since 3-0 -- and 3-pointers by Alex Caruso and Gilgeous-Alexander extended it to 70-64 after three quarters. Oklahoma City pushed the advantage to 93-76 on a 3 by Gilgeous-Alexander to give him 17 points with 1:44 left. He then asked to be taken out during a timeout and did not return to the game.

Jalen Williams scored 21 points, and Chet Holmgren had 12 points and 17 rebounds for the Thunder.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

Brooklyn Nets vs. Cleveland Cavaliers


              Cleveland; Saturday, 7:30 p.m. EDT


              BOTTOM LINE: Brooklyn takes on Cleveland in Eastern Conference action Saturday.


              Cleveland went 52-30 overall and 33-19 in Eastern Conference action a season ago. The Cavaliers averaged 18.4 points off of turnovers, 15.1 second-chance points and 33.4 bench points last season.


              Brooklyn finished 20-62 overall and 14-37 in Eastern Conference action during the 2025-26 season. The Nets averaged 8.0 steals, 4.3 blocks and 15.0 turnovers per game last season.


              INJURIES: Cavaliers: Nae'Qwan Tomlin: out (back), Khalifa Diop: day to day (knee).
